distinguishing_features: Injecting alkaline scrubber slurry directly at the duct wall interface to neutralize condensed acid
Using exothermic neutralization heat to locally raise wall temperature above the acid dew-point
Active pH control via existing FGD DCS/chemistry instrumentation rather than temperature/feed-gas setpoint changes
Targeting FGD duct carbon-steel corrosion rather than catalyst-bed plugging by acid mist
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent sulfuric/sulfurous acid condensate corrosion on carbon-steel FGD duct surfaces without passive liners or duct material upgrades, using active local neutralization and dew-point suppression.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated heat release is orders of magnitude too small to raise the wall temperature above the acid dew-point, so the claimed thermal mechanism is physically implausible and the proposed validation cannot confirm the stated corrosion suppression.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying alkaline chemical dosing to prevent acid corrosion and raising temperature above a dew-point are both standard, routine measures already suggested by the closest prior art, with only a change of chemical and target equipment.
